correctness.rationale: Proof supplies the complete chronological forcing sequence with (m-1)k seeds for arbitrary arm lengths; an explicit integer symmetric matrix has exact graph-power support and an (m-1)k-dimensional kernel obtained from k degrees of freedom on each arm and k independent total-sum equations. The standard maximum-nullity/zero-forcing inequality closes the bounds. The self-contained verifier checked 53 exact rational matrix/force instances plus 10,981 subminimal seeds.

originality.rationale: The 2026 graph-powers paper explicitly leaves equality for equal-arm spider powers as Conjecture 10 (after only proving an upper bound); the explicit nonnegative-integer matrix proving the lower bound for arbitrary unequal arms is not contained in the inspected primary work. The earlier path-power and tree-square formulas cover only acknowledged boundary instances. No indexed or web-identified statement was found that implies the general result; residual priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: A poorly indexed or unpublished real-minimum-rank construction might already imply the same higher-power identity.
Two relevant indexed records were available as published summaries but their linked full manuscripts were not accessible; the non-implication judgement for these is limited to their stated scopes.
The result has not been independently audited; exhaustive finite tests do not establish novelty or replace proof.

value.rationale: The exact theorem resolves a named 2026 conjecture about zero forcing of graph powers in all higher-power cases and strengthens the equal-arm hypothesis to arbitrary unequal arms. An explicit symmetric integer matrix simultaneously determines the real minimum rank, providing a structural explanation rather than a routine parameter substitution.
